title: implementation-verification — plan 001
epic_title: Build codegate — the verification harness (stage-8 local CI)

tasks.title: Define the closed schemas, the check registry, and the ecosystem defaults substrate
tasks.goal: The harness's data substrate exists and holds its invariants: a manifest that parses closed, a verdict that is atomic, revision-bound, and state-exclusive, and a registry that derives the ladder from self-registered checks.
tasks.current: No verification code exists; `internal/verify` is empty ground.
tasks.desired: The manifest schema parses closed (unknown keys are errors) with verb bindings, test globs, per-verb env entries (names passed or values pinned), time bounds, state dirs, and the baseline path; the verdict type carries per-rung and per-check results, findings, and the six bindings (head sha, resolved diff base, manifest hash, baseline hash, codegate version, git version), writes atomically, and enforces its state invariants; checks self-register with rung, verb dependencies, author-independence class, and input set; ecosystem defaults (globs, skip/assertion patterns, secret/artifact rules, failure-identity parsers, state-dir and cache-pin defaults) compile in as versioned data the manifest overrides.
scope: The manifest, verdict, and finding types with closed parsing and the atomic temp+rename write.
Property tests for the verdict invariants: bindings present, pass-class excludes fail/error and `skip:not-reached`, rung-and-check completeness.
The check registry with per-file init() self-registration and ladder derivation.
The compiled ecosystem-defaults tables with manifest-override resolution.
out_of_scope: Any check logic or verb execution — later tasks register real checks.
The CLI surface — T2's task.
acceptance: A manifest with an unknown key fails closed-parse; a manifest declaring only a stack and a baseline path resolves the full verb set from ecosystem defaults.
Property tests prove no verdict instance combines a pass-class state with any fail or error check result or a `skip:not-reached` rung.
A demonstration check lands as one new file with zero shared-line edits, and the derived ladder includes it.
An interrupted write (kill between temp and rename) leaves no verdict artifact.

tasks.title: The run subcommand shell: invocation contract, bindings, and refusals
tasks.goal: `codegate run` implements the subprocess contract's edges: every invalid invocation refuses fail-closed before any verb executes, valid invocations resolve their bindings, and exactly one invocation holds a workspace at a time.
tasks.current: T1's substrate exists but nothing is invocable; there is no binary entry point.
tasks.desired: `codegate run --workspace --diff-base [--incremental]` refuses with exit 2 and a configuration-error verdict on any invalid, ambiguous, or flag-like-positional invocation, a missing or unparseable manifest, a malformed bound baseline, a dirty workspace (codegate scratch excepted), or a below-floor system git; the verdict is stdout-carried when the workspace flag itself is the defect, artifact-plus-stdout otherwise; a valid invocation resolves the six bindings (diff base resolved to a sha) and holds an flock-held descriptor — a concurrent invocation refuses busy; exit classes 0–3 are wired.
scope: Invocation parsing with the full refusal matrix (I3 discipline) and exit-class wiring.
Clean-tree assertion, git-version floor check, and bindings resolution.
The configuration-error verdict emission rule (artifact vs stdout-carried).
The flock workspace lock with busy refusal.
out_of_scope: Running any rung — the ladder body is T3.
Residue reaping and kill-recovery beyond the lock's kernel release — T9.
acceptance: Every malformed-invocation class (unknown mode, missing/ambiguous workspace or diff base, flag-like positional, dirty tree) refuses with exit 2 before any verb executes.
The workspace-flag-defect fixture yields a stdout-carried configuration-error verdict; the malformed-manifest and malformed-baseline fixtures yield artifact verdicts naming the defect.
A second concurrent invocation on the same workspace refuses busy while the first completes normally.
A valid invocation's verdict records all six bindings with the diff base resolved to a sha.
key_interfaces: `Invocation` (parsed contract), `Bindings` (the six-field set), `WorkspaceLock` (flock semantics); exit-class constants.

tasks.title: The bounded verb runner and the repo-verb ladder (rungs 0, 1, 4)
tasks.goal: The ladder runs end to end on a fixture repo: repo verbs execute env-stripped and time-bounded, a failing rung returns compact findings without executing later rungs, and the verdict enumerates everything.
tasks.current: Invocations resolve and refuse correctly (T2) but no rung executes; no verdict has ever contained a real check result.
tasks.desired: The runner executes a verb with an environment built only from the manifest's per-verb entries, kills it at its bound plus the recorded grace, and distinguishes spawn failure and timeout (rung error, exit 3) from check failure (red, exit 1); format/lint (rung 0), build (rung 1), and exec-probe (rung 4) checks run via the registry in latency order with first-failure stop; findings carry check id, class, rung, file:line where the class has one, a one-line message, and full output by reference in scratch; an unbound verb's check records `skip:verb-absent`, aggregates the rung as pass-with-skips, and drives green-degraded; unreached rungs record `skip:not-reached`.
scope: The bounded runner: env construction (names + pinned values), wall-clock bound + grace, UB-1/UB-2 error classes.
The four repo-verb check units and ladder execution with first-failure stop.
Finding emission with log-by-reference scratch retention.
The Go fixture repo driving red, green, green-degraded, and error paths.
out_of_scope: The verbless neutral checks — T4.
Write-scope enforcement (Landlock) — T9; this task ships strip + bounds only.
acceptance: A rung-0 lint failure returns findings with file:line and zero rung-1+ verb executions recorded; the probe-less fixture yields green-degraded with `skip:verb-absent` recorded.
A fixture verb reading an ambient env var observes it absent; a pinned-value entry is observed; a hanging verb terminates at bound+grace with rung result error-timeout.
A missing verb binary yields rung error class `infra` (exit 3), never red or green.
Every completed run's verdict enumerates all configured rungs and checks, including `skip:not-reached` after an early stop.
key_interfaces: `Runner.Exec(verb, bounds, env) → Result`; `Ladder.Run(bindings, mode) → Verdict`; the finding schema's field set (the joint feedback contract's v1 shape).

tasks.title: The verbless rung-0 checks: secret scan, forbidden artifacts, machinery protection
tasks.goal: The three checks needing no repo capability catch what they exist to catch, diff-scoped: a seeded secret, a committed binary or baked absolute path, and a proposal diff touching verification machinery.
tasks.current: Rung 0 runs only the repo's own format/lint verbs (T3); the harness brings no checks of its own.
tasks.desired: The proposal diff (resolved diff base → head) is extracted once and shared; the secret scan matches ecosystem-table patterns over added lines; forbidden-artifact rules flag binary content, size-threshold breaches, and baked absolute paths in added content; machinery protection derives its path set — the manifest's own path, its declared paths, the acquisition-pin path, and the verdict/scratch path — and reds any proposal diff touching one; all three run inside rung 0's latency budget.
scope: Proposal-diff extraction with rename detection as the shared substrate.
The three check units registered on rung 0, rules sourced from ecosystem tables with the manifest extension point.
The derived machinery path set (never hand-kept).
Latency measurement hooks for NFR-1's rung-0 budget.
out_of_scope: Test-file analysis of any kind — rung 3's tasks (T6, T7).
Tree-scoped (non-diff) scanning — deliberately diff-scoped per the design.
acceptance: A seeded secret in the proposal diff reds rung 0 with a class-named finding; the same secret pre-existing in the tree (outside the diff) does not.
A committed binary and a baked absolute path each red rung 0 with class-named findings.

Catch seed 3 — a baseline addition and separately a manifest verb-unbinding riding a proposal diff — reds with a machinery finding naming the path; a pin-downgrade diff reds the same way; a non-machinery diff never triggers it.
Rung-0 wall-time on the fixture and dogfood repos is measured and recorded in EVT-1 timings (the NFR-1 evidence hook).
key_interfaces: `DiffSet` (added lines, file status, renames); `MachineryPaths(bindings) → set`; ecosystem rule-table entries for secrets and artifacts.

tasks.title: Rung 2: the test verb, the no-new-failures baseline, and capture-baseline
tasks.goal: Rung 2 adjudicates honestly on healthy and red-main repos alike: any failure reds a baseline-less repo, only new failures red a baseline-bound one, shrinkage is recorded, and the baseline is born from an operator-run subcommand — never from run mode.
tasks.current: The test verb executes like any repo verb (T3) but its result is exit-code-only; no baseline semantics exist.
tasks.desired: With no baseline bound, any test failure reds rung 2; with a baseline bound, failure identities parse via the stack's ecosystem parser and the rung evaluates no-new-failures — failing on any failure absent from the baseline, recording observed shrinkage in the verdict; unparseable output with a baseline bound is a rung error, never an exit-code fallback; `codegate capture-baseline` runs the test verb, writes the baseline file (failure identities + capture provenance) at the manifest-declared path, and exits — run mode never writes it.
scope: The rung-2 check with both evaluation modes and shrink recording.
Failure-identity parsing for the Go stack via the ecosystem table (further stacks ride T10's fixtures).
The baseline file format with capture provenance, and UB-9's fail-closed path.
The `capture-baseline` subcommand with the DINV-6 write discipline.
out_of_scope: Baseline growth enforcement beyond FR-8's machinery flag — human-lane by convention until the remote phase.
Detection-assisted capture — the basis's WR-6.
acceptance: A clean fixture passes and one seeded failing test reds rung 2 with no baseline bound; the red-main fixture (K pre-existing failures) passes with zero new failures and reds when one new failure is seeded.
A baseline-shrink run records the shrink in the verdict's rung-2 entry.
Garbage test output with a baseline bound yields rung-2 error; the same output with no baseline follows the exit-code path.
`capture-baseline` produces a baseline the red-main fixture binds; a write-audit test proves run mode performs zero writes to manifest or baseline.
key_interfaces: `BaselineFile` (identities + provenance), `EvaluateRung2(result, baseline) → RungResult` with shrink record; `FailureIdentityParser` per stack.

tasks.title: Falsification: the ephemeral worktree and the two-leg protocol
tasks.goal: Tautological tests are caught mechanically and legitimate diffs pass untouched: the falsification check proves new tests discriminate implementation presence, in a throwaway worktree the agent's tree never feels.
tasks.current: Rung 3 does not exist; a test asserting nothing sails green (the basis's named top-risk class).
tasks.desired: When the proposal diff's non-test half is non-empty and test files were added or modified, codegate creates a worktree at the workspace HEAD under a run-id-unique scratch path, provisions the manifest's declared state dirs, and runs two legs — sanity (unreverted: the targeted tests must pass, else rung error) then revert (reverse of the non-test half applied: tests passing without the implementation produce a falsification finding naming each) — focused where the stack's runner supports it; test-only or no-new-test diffs record not-applicable and emit nothing; a revert that does not apply is a rung error; the worktree is removed at run end and the workspace tree hash is byte-identical after every run.
scope: The ephemeral-worktree lifecycle: run-id path, state-dir provisioning, removal.
The two-leg protocol with the environment-vs-discrimination distinction.
The FR-18 applicability rule and its not-applicable recording.
The UB-4 inapplicable-revert error path.
out_of_scope: The test-delta audit — T7 (a sibling check on the same rung).
Stale-worktree pruning after kills — T9's janitor.
acceptance: Catch seed 1 (a tautological test) reds rung 3 with a falsification finding naming the test.
The refactor-only and mixed-with-genuine-tests fixtures pass without findings; the test-only fixture records falsification not-applicable while its test-delta audit still evaluates.
A worktree whose sanity leg fails (a state-dir deliberately withheld) yields rung error — never a falsification verdict.
After every rung-3 run — pass, red, or error — the workspace tree hash is byte-identical to before.
key_interfaces: `EphemeralWorktree{Create, Provision, Remove}`; `Falsify(diffset, worktree) → CheckResult` implementing the two-leg order.

tasks.title: The test-delta audit: deletion, skip-marker, and assertion-removal floors
tasks.goal: Silencing a test costs a named finding: deletions, skip markers, and hollowed assertions in the proposal diff are flagged structurally, and renames pass clean.
tasks.current: A diff deleting or skip-marking a failing test changes nothing the harness sees; silence is free.
tasks.desired: Over the shared diff set (T4's substrate), deletions of test-glob paths, added skip/exclusion markers, and modified tests whose assertion-pattern count drops each produce a test-delta finding naming the affected test; git rename detection runs first so moves and renames never fire the floors; all patterns are per-stack ecosystem-table data.
scope: The test-delta check registered on rung 3, all three trigger classes.
The per-stack skip-marker and assertion-pattern tables for the Go stack.
Rename-safety via the diff set's rename detection.
out_of_scope: Detection depth beyond the three-class floor — the design's Q2, grown by data PR.
Any test execution — this check is purely structural.
acceptance: Catch seed 2 reds in each of its three classes: a deleted failing test, an added skip marker, and an assertion-removal (hollowed test), each finding naming the test.
The rename/move-refactor fixture passes without a test-delta finding.
Pattern-table additions require zero changes to the check unit (data-only growth proven by a test adding a pattern).
key_interfaces: `TestDelta(diffset, tables) → []Finding`; ecosystem table entries `SkipMarkers`, `AssertionPatterns` keyed by stack.

tasks.title: Incremental re-verification: the prior verdict as the only state
tasks.goal: A fix cycle re-verifies without re-running the world and without ever laundering a stale result: the prior verdict is the sole state, and any doubt means a full run.
tasks.current: Every invocation runs the full ladder; the loop pays the whole suite per fix.
tasks.desired: `--incremental` reads the workspace's prior verdict; it qualifies only when every binding except the head revision matches (resolved diff base, manifest hash, baseline hash, codegate version, git version) and it parses — otherwise full run; the re-run set is the previously-failed rung first, plus every rung not recorded pass, plus every rung whose registry-declared input set changed under `git diff <prior head>`; only prior passes with unchanged inputs carry, marked `carried-from <run id>`; conservative v1 input defaults (whole tree for repo-verb rungs, the diff composition for rung 3) hold, with first-failure ordering as the stated primary economy.
scope: Prior-verdict qualification with the full-binding match rule.
Re-run-set computation from recorded results + input sets, and carried-pass marking.
The invalidation fixtures: changed manifest, baseline, diff base, and codegate version each force a full run.
out_of_scope: Sub-rung (per-test) caching — a future supersession by design.
Any second state artifact — the verdict is the only state, structurally.
acceptance: A fixture fix-cycle re-verifies with strictly fewer verb runs than the initial full ladder, and its carried passes carry `carried-from` provenance.
Changing any single binding (manifest, baseline, diff base, codegate version) forces a full run.
A prior verdict containing a `skip:not-reached` or failed rung re-runs that rung — a pass-class verdict never emerges containing a never-run rung.
A missing or unparseable prior verdict silently degrades to a full run (never an error).
key_interfaces: `PlanIncremental(prior Verdict, bindings, diff) → RerunSet`; `CarriedPass{FromRunID}` in the verdict schema.

tasks.title: Runtime hardening: write-scope enforcement, kill-idempotence, and the janitors
tasks.goal: The runner's security posture and the AP-12 residue discipline become real: out-of-scope writes fail on the enforced platform, kills leave nothing wedged, and every throwaway resource has its janitor.
tasks.current: Verbs run stripped and bounded (T3) but writes anywhere succeed; a killed run leaves a registered worktree and old scratch accumulates.
tasks.desired: On Linux the runner confines verb writes to workspace + scratch via Landlock — an out-of-scope write fails the rung as error with a violation-classed finding; on macOS the posture is strip + redirection with the residual named (the A-6 write-scope leg pins to the Linux CI matrix); kill-mid-run — including during rung 3 — leaves no verdict artifact, the flock releases on death, and the next invocation prunes codegate's own stale worktree registrations and drops older run scratch per the retention rule; shared-`.git` worktree operations treat transient git-lock failures as rung errors, fail-closed.
scope: The Landlock confinement behind a platform seam, with the violation finding class.
Kill-recovery: no partial verdict, lock release, next-run equality with an uninterrupted run.
The janitors: stale-worktree pruning by run-id namespace and scratch retention.
The macOS residual posture, documented in-code where the seam degrades.
out_of_scope: Any second enforcement backend (bwrap-class) — rejected by design for NFR-3.
Env-strip and time bounds — shipped in T3; this task adds only the write scope and residue discipline.
acceptance: On the Linux CI matrix, a fixture verb writing outside workspace+scratch fails the rung with a violation finding; the same fixture on macOS records the documented residual behavior.
Kill-mid-run (including during rung 3) leaves no verdict artifact; the subsequent run prunes the stale worktree registration and equals an uninterrupted run.
Scratch from runs older than the retention rule is absent after the next invocation; the prior verdict always survives.
A concurrent sibling workspace's rung-3 run on the same clone proceeds; a transient git-lock collision yields a rung error, never a hang or corruption.
key_interfaces: `Confine(cmd, allowedPaths)` behind the platform seam; `PruneStaleWorktrees(scratchNS)`; the scratch retention constant recorded in the verdict schema.

tasks.title: The multi-stack fixture matrix and the permanent catch suite
tasks.goal: Technology-independence and the anti-gaming bar become tested properties: the identical harness binds and adjudicates three stacks, and every adversarial seed family stays permanently blocked in CI.
tasks.current: Every check is proven on the Go fixture only; FR-16's zero-per-stack-code claim and M2's 3/3 catch bar are asserted, not demonstrated.
tasks.desired: Two additional fixture repos (distinct non-Go stacks) carry minimal manifests and exercise the full ladder — bind, red, green, green-degraded, baseline, falsification (with state-dir provisioning), and test-delta paths — through ecosystem defaults alone; the catch suite runs all seed families (tautology; silenced test in three classes; machinery edits including the pin downgrade) paired with the legitimate-diff fixtures, on all three stacks where the seed applies, as a permanent CI job emitting EVT-4.
scope: The two non-Go fixture repos with manifests, scripted verbs, and failure-identity parser entries.
The matrix driver proving the ladder end to end per stack with zero per-stack code in `internal/verify` (inspection hook included).
The permanent catch-suite job wiring EVT-4 results in the harness's CI.
out_of_scope: Real second-repo onboarding — fixtures stand in by design.
The advisory parity workflow — T11.
acceptance: The fixture matrix runs the full ladder on three stacks in CI, green, with an inspection note proving stack-specific behavior lives only in manifest data and ecosystem tables.
The catch suite blocks every seed family case — including assertion-removal and the pin-downgrade machinery seed — and the paired legitimate fixtures pass, on every applicable stack.
Rung-3 legs (sanity + revert) run on all three stacks, proving state-dir provisioning per stack.
The suite is a required job in the harness's own CI and emits per-seed EVT-4 records.
key_interfaces: Fixture-repo layout convention (manifest + scripted verbs + seeds); the matrix/catch drivers' table-driven entry points.

tasks.title: The release lane, the acquisition pin, and the advisory parity dry-run
tasks.goal: codegate ships the way the repo-layout conventions demand and proves its portability constraint: pinned static artifacts, an owned pin section, and one advisory headless CI run whose verdict matches a local run rung for rung.
tasks.current: codegate builds from source only; no release artifacts, no pin section, no evidence the identical harness runs headless in CI.
tasks.desired: The release lane produces sha256-pinned static binaries per version; the operand acquisition config's closed schema gains the additive `codegate:` section (version + sha256) with the shim resolution path; an advisory (explicitly non-blocking) GitHub Actions job runs the identical harness headless on a commit and the comparison records rung-for-rung verdict parity with a local run (EVT-5); the living rollups gain the shipped capability's entries including the verdict-state and troubleshooting reference.
scope: The goreleaser-style release configuration for codegate artifacts.
The additive pin-section schema change with shim resolution.
The advisory dry-run workflow + the parity comparison recording EVT-5.
The living-doc entries (techspec/prd rollups; verdict-state reference).
out_of_scope: Required-check registration or any enforcement semantics — the basis's WR-5, deliberately parked.
Publishing cadence policy — releases cut when the operator tags.
acceptance: A release build produces static, sha256-pinned codegate artifacts resolvable through the shim against the new pin section.
The pin section parses closed alongside the existing tool section; a wrong sha fails resolution fail-closed.
The advisory workflow runs the identical harness headless and records rung-for-rung parity with a local verdict on the same commit (EVT-5), and is visibly non-blocking.
The living rollups document the shipped capability: subcommands, verdict states, finding classes, and the troubleshooting reference.
key_interfaces: The `codegate:` pin-section schema; the dry-run workflow's parity comparison step; the release artifact naming convention.
touches: the operand acquisition config schema (additive codegate section)

deferred.reason: verified at Phase-B integration, not buildable here: the VerificationGate port and its adapter land on implement-now's ledger via the queued P-1 legs (additive amendment + design supersession there + the NR-2 corrective amendment on this basis) — this plan builds the harness side only, and its CLI contract is fully testable without the host (design:codegate-v1 §3.11, R3)
